# Offline training (Chase)

Code: `ml/src/fitness_ml/training/` (CLI `fitness-train`). Nothing here runs during the live demo; the laptop loads exported artifacts from `ml/models/`.

**Status: implemented, not yet run.** No dataset has been downloaded, no model trained, no metric produced. Every number you report must come from `metrics_*.json` generated by `fitness-train evaluate`.

```bash
.venv/bin/pip install -e 'ml[train]'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-ml download-model
```

## Data layout (all git-ignored)

```
ml/data/raw/mydeadlift/          # unzip MyDeadlift here
ml/data/raw/multiview/           # unzip Multi-View Fitness here
ml/data/manifest*.csv            # one row per video: participant, view, exercise, variation, labels
ml/data/cache/*.npz              # MediaPipe landmarks per video (no pixels)
ml/data/splits.json              # participant lists per split
ml/models/<model_version>/       # metadata.json + model.joblib|model.pt + metrics_test.json
```

Sources (both CC BY 4.0; credit them in the demo):
- MyDeadlift — https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/w5prmmxyt9/1 — `GB|PB|LLK_S<subject>_R<rep>.mp4`. GB = correct, PB = rounded back, LLK = knees beyond toes. 7 subjects, side view, 1 rep per clip.
- Multi-View Fitness — https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/kgbb3yn47p/3 — 26 subjects, 7 exercises, front/side/diagonal, good/bad. The same videos appear in 3 folder layouts; point the adapter at **one** (e.g. `Dataset Subject-wise`). It de-dupes by name + size anyway.

## Pipeline

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train ingest mydeadlift --root ml/data/raw/mydeadlift --out ml/data/manifest_mydeadlift.csv
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train ingest multiview --root "ml/data/raw/multiview/Dataset Subject-wise" --out ml/data/manifest_multiview.csv
```

`ingest` prints counts per dataset/exercise/variation/view/label and **lists every file it couldn't label**, exiting 1. Multi-View's file naming isn't documented, so check the first run's skip list and adjust `MULTIVIEW_EXERCISES` / `SUBJECT` in `manifest.py` if the folder names differ from what's assumed. Only pass `--allow-skips` once the skipped files are confirmed to be non-training files.

Your own consented clips: write a CSV with columns `video_id,path,dataset,participant_id,camera_view,exercise,variation,form_label,issue_label,license`, then run `fitness-train ingest csv --root my_clips.csv --out ml/data/manifest_own.csv`.

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train merge ml/data/manifest_mydeadlift.csv ml/data/manifest_multiview.csv --out ml/data/manifest.csv
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train extract --limit 3
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train extract
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train split --test-participants mydeadlift-S04,mydeadlift-S07
```

The split is made on **participants, per dataset, before windowing**. MyDeadlift's official test subjects are pinned; the other datasets get a seeded random 20% of people for test and 15% for val. The split records the manifest hash, and training refuses a manifest that changed afterwards.

### Exercise recognition (curl / squat / deadlift / other)

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train train --task recognition --model rf
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train train --task recognition --model knn
```

### Form, per exercise

- `form_binary`: good/bad, from Multi-View and MyDeadlift. At runtime this becomes a *measurement* (`form_model_p_bad`), never a correction.
- `form_issue`: specific labelled errors (MyDeadlift: `none` / `rounded_back` / `knees_past_toes`). At runtime these become issue codes like `deadlift.rounded_back` with `provenance: trained_model`. The backend only voices codes in its approved cue table, so these won't be spoken unless Tyler adds them deliberately.

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train train --task form_issue --exercise deadlift --model rf
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train train --task form_binary --exercise squat --model rf
```

### GRU comparator (optional)

```bash
.venv/bin/pip install -e 'ml[train,gru]'
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train train --task recognition --model gru --device auto
```

It uses the same windows and the same split, with a fixed seed, early stopping on val macro-F1, and the best checkpoint exported to `model.pt`. The checkpoint loads on CPU. GPU instructions are in `docs/VULTR_TRAINING.md`.

### Evaluate (held-out people from the artifact's own metadata)

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-train evaluate --artifact ml/models/<model_version>
```

`metrics_test.json` holds:
- per-class precision/recall/F1/support, macro-F1 and the confusion matrix
- macro-F1 per camera view and per dataset
- per-video majority-vote accuracy
- a rejection sweep: coverage, accuracy on accepted windows, `other` accepted as a supported exercise, supported windows rejected
- for form models, the false-correction rate

Choose `Config.reject_below` from the rejection sweep, not by taste.

## Use a model live

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-ml run --source live --exercise curl --recognizer ml/models/<recognition_version>
```

```bash
.venv/bin/fitness-ml run --source recorded --video clip.mp4 --exercise deadlift --form-model ml/models/<form_version>
```

The artifact's `feature_names` must match the current code, or loading fails with the code revision it needs.
